claim: The hosted v0.1.0 tarball installs and runs in a fresh project.
where: landing install section, demo snippet, README
sandbox: download the served tarball into a new npm project, install it, and run its exported scheduler

claim: The tarball contains working ESM and CommonJS builds, React builds, declarations, and preset CSS.
sandbox: install the downloaded tarball in a fresh project, import and require it, and inspect every declared target

claim: The package provides TypeScript declarations for its core public API.
sandbox: compile a strict NodeNext TypeScript consumer against the downloaded tarball

claim: The package and all four views are MIT licensed.
sandbox: inspect the package manifest, LICENSE, and built release file

claim: The core package has no runtime dependencies and React is optional.
sandbox: inspect dependencies and optional peer metadata in package.json

claim: The demo runs the v0.1.0 package build and shows a matching fresh-project snippet.
sandbox: open ?demo=1, assert the version marker and snippet, and verify the site build aliases the built package

claim: The README scheduler example moves an event while preserving its duration.
sandbox: run the documented data and assert the moved resource, start, and end

claim: The scheduler provides create, update, move, resize, and remove operations without mutating prior state.
sandbox: run every operation and compare the original frozen state after all changes

claim: Resource timeline models return slots and clipped event positions as percentages.
sandbox: build a ten-hour timeline containing an event clipped at the start

claim: Time-grid models assign collision columns to overlapping events.
sandbox: lay out two overlapping events and assert their columns and shared model output

claim: The package returns six-week months and finite continuous-month windows.
sandbox: build an August grid and an overscanned month window with explicit finite limits

claim: The demo renders day, week, continuous month, and resource timeline views.
where: landing first screen and how it works, README
sandbox: open a fresh demo, select every named view, and assert its rendered model

claim: The demo views use the same edited scheduler state.
sandbox: edit an event, switch from timeline to day and back, and assert the edit in both views

claim: Demo edits stay in memory and clear on reset, reload, or exit.
where: landing first screen, demo banner, privacy, README
sandbox: fresh ?demo=1 context; edit, reset, reload, exit, re-enter, and inspect cookies and persistent storage

claim: Pointer helpers create, move, resize-start, and resize-end at fixed intervals.
where: README pointer input and public API
sandbox: commit all four pointer modes against one event and assert exact timestamps

claim: Pointer helpers capture the active pointer, snap movement, and reject invalid scale or interval values.
sandbox: move beyond the origin, assert pointer capture and snapped output, then test zero, negative, NaN, and infinity

claim: Grid navigation maps Arrow, Home, End, Page Up, and Page Down keys to bounded cells.
where: README pointer input and public API
sandbox: assert every documented key and an unhandled key against a fixed grid

claim: Demo events move and resize by keyboard in 15-minute steps with a live result message.
sandbox: move and resize a focused sample event, then assert its accessible name and live message

claim: Public event dates require ISO date-time strings with Z or an offset.
sandbox: reject locale and offset-free values, then accept an explicit offset

claim: Configured day boundaries follow DST and non-DST time zones.
sandbox: assert spring, fall, and Asia/Kolkata day boundaries

claim: The package supports built-in, Temporal, and caller-supplied date-fns calculations.
where: README date calculations and public API
sandbox: run the built-in adapter, Temporal polyfill adapter, and supplied date functions

claim: Version 0.1 does not expand recurring events.
sandbox: pass one event with a recurrence rule and assert that one unchanged event remains

claim: Version 0.1 has no storage, account, payment, iCal, print, Vue, or Svelte modules.
where: landing scope section, terms, README support
sandbox: inspect every built export and the package export map for excluded product modules

claim: The package build targets ES2022 and pointer interactions use the Pointer Events API.
sandbox: inspect the package build target and run the demo in a browser with PointerEvent support

claim: The package exports preset CSS with hs-* hooks and overridable color variables.
sandbox: install the tarball, load its CSS, override --hs-accent, and assert the computed event color

claim: The optional React adapter renders with React 18 and React 19.
sandbox: install the tarball separately with React 18.3.1 and 19.1.0, then server-render HeadlessScheduler

claim: The site loads no analytics, third-party scripts, or remote fonts and writes no cookies or persistent app storage.
where: landing privacy section, privacy route, README
sandbox: intercept a complete ?demo=1 flow and inspect origins, cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, and IndexedDB

claim: The core package makes no network or browser-storage calls; the application controls persistence.
sandbox: instrument fetch and browser-storage globals while importing and exercising the built package

claim: The core returns serializable scheduling data without requiring or rendering a DOM.
where: landing first screen and how it works, README introduction and styling
sandbox: import the built package without document, build a timeline, and serialize its returned model

claim: The service worker caches local pages and assets so the sample demo opens offline after its first visit.
where: demo offline state, README privacy and verification sections
sandbox: fresh ?demo=1 context; inspect same-origin cache entries, go offline, reload, and assert seeded UI

claim: Demo, privacy, terms, and not-found states have real responses, route metadata, focus, and announcements.
sandbox: inspect raw route HTML and status, then navigate with History API and assert title, focus, and live text

claim: The built static site contains the legal routes, demo, service worker, and installable tarball.
sandbox: serve only dist/site, request each public artifact, and assert generated files
